block.title: Cheaper calls take the λANF backend from 4.1× to 3.6× ocamlopt on rx.ir
block.p: Every call between lowered functions paid for a prologue, an epilogue and arguments on the stack. This round cut that cost in Regs.v, which compiles everything nanofil-backend compile-allocated takes, and in AnfLower.v:

ul.li: A function of local linkage that returns in registers has a private entry for the module's direct calls, which takes the first two stack words in %rsi and %rax. Its fast entry loads them and falls into it.
A function whose body calls nothing links no Fil-C frame. Its failure blocks link the frame before they call the runtime's reporter.
The catching origin is stored once at the entry, and a pollcheck's slow path restores it. Before, every call stored it.
The entry no longer zeroes the roots that the incoming arguments fill.
A lowered function returns its value and the young index in two registers.
Arena checks are at alignment 1, so they test no alignment.

claim.p: On all 53 IR fixtures, for compile, compile-promoted and compile-allocated, the arena build prints the same assembly, stderr and exit status as the OCaml build: 0 of 159 runs differ.

metrics.baseline: ocamlopt build of the same backend

block.p: That is still short of M3's 2×. Calls, prologues and epilogues take about 23% of the time on rx.ir. Bounds checks take 11%, spills 12% and arena address arithmetic 9%. Every lowered function takes five values: the arena, the state, the young index, the roots' top and the nursery's end. The two pointers fill the fast convention's four argument registers, and all five compete for the seven register homes. Moving the state into the arena's object would free a home and two argument words, but it changes the runtime's layout.

nanofil -O does not use Regs.v, so the benchmark gate's builds are unchanged. When the gate's Lua, zlib and bzip2 workloads are built through compile-allocated, they give the same output as before. None got slower: Lua's int and tab scripts got 6% and 4% faster, and the rest stayed within noise.
